quote: can this be done via email?
stewart_read: Rep answered the intro but never got a real interest/verify start before the customer took control of the call's direction with a channel demand.
coaching_implication: A tighter intro into verify questions (even one line) before the customer can redirect might have kept the rep in control of the flow.

quote: I know plenty about solar, so I'm not worried about any of that. I just wanna know what price you guys can get me at
stewart_read: Customer discloses prior solar company conversations unprompted; rep never asks which companies or what he saw.
coaching_implication: Probing 'who else have you talked to, what did they quote' would surface competitive context and could reframe the email-only ask.

quote: what is your warranty on the panels and, that stuff
stewart_read: Customer is pulling the rep into closer-tier product/pricing content; the rep never redirects with the escape hatch line.
coaching_implication: Rep should have used 'that's exactly what our specialist is built to answer' to redirect instead of letting the ask sit unaddressed and continuing to negotiate channel.

quote: what if I cut the in person appointment and I all that sit down stuff? If I remove that and I set you up with just a phone call
stewart_read: Customer's real objection is 'I don't want to waste time / send me proposal by email' — a scripted rebuttal exists (rebuttals.send_proposal_before_meeting) but rep improvises a workaround instead of the canonical hold-the-line reframe.
alternative_hypothesis: Reactive read: rep is genuinely trying to save the appointment by offering a lighter-touch phone call, which is a reasonable improvisation given the customer's stated time pressure.
coaching_implication: Use the canonical proposal-before-meeting response with a value reason (explanation prevents confusion) rather than negotiating format on the fly.

quote: If that's something that you guys can't do, then I'll just rather not deal with it and then just move on.
stewart_read: Second touch of the same email-only demand, now with an explicit ultimatum; rep still doesn't answer directly and instead asks 'can I ask you something?' before pivoting to reassurance about being 'one of the best.'
coaching_implication: This is the moment to hold the line explicitly ('we don't email proposals because...') rather than reassurance-only ('you're gonna love our offer').

quote: I want that just in an email.
stewart_read: Third touch, near-verbatim repeat of the original ask; rep responds with more bill-collection urgency ('get that bill real quick') instead of resolving the channel question.
coaching_implication: Same coaching as prior touches — this is the same unresolved objection recurring a third time with no new rep angle.

quote: I literally am not allowed to just email because I don't have anything needed.
stewart_read: Rep finally states the actual policy constraint directly, but only after the customer has already said goodbye twice — too late to change the outcome.
coaching_implication: This exact line, delivered on touch one, would have given the customer a real reason instead of three rounds of vague workarounds.
